fact: For finite real D>0, the positive reals s<D have supremum D; if Q∈[0,∞] satisfies Q≥s+1 for every such s, then Q≥D+1.
justification: This is a routine ordered-field endpoint completion of the stated supremum argument, not an additional dimension theorem. D is an upper bound. Given real r<D, put m=max(0,r) and s=(m+D)/2; then 0<s<D and r<s. For the shifted conclusion, Q=∞ is immediate. If Q<D+1, it has a finite real value q≥0. Now m=max(0,q-1)<D and s=(m+D)/2 satisfies 0<s<D and s+1>q, contradicting the available lower bound Q≥s+1. These explicit midpoint inequalities require only elementary arithmetic and order; there is no limit exchange or extra hypothesis.

grounds.reason: L1 supplies D>0 and N002 supplies finiteness; F001 proves Q=dim_H(F)≥s+1 for arbitrary 0<s<D.
dim_H has codomain [0,∞], so a value below finite D+1 is finite and nonnegative.
D is finite and may be viewed as a nonnegative real.
